prompt: We're a German government agency (Bundesbehörde) and we need to build a private cloud for processing VS-NfD (Verschlusssache - Nur für den Dienstgebrauch) data. We must comply with BSI IT-Grundschutz and achieve C5 attestation. We want to use OpenStack and are considering whether we can use FLOSS components throughout or whether we need BSI-approved products for certain layers. Our data must stay within Germany. What architecture do you recommend, and how do we navigate the BSI accreditation process?

assertions.name: german_classification_levels
assertions.description: Correctly names German classification levels (VS-NfD, VS-VERTRAULICH, GEHEIM, STRENG GEHEIM)

assertions.name: bsi_grundschutz
assertions.description: Addresses BSI IT-Grundschutz methodology in detail (not just mentions it — explains what it requires)

assertions.name: c5_attestation
assertions.description: Explains the C5 (Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue) attestation process

assertions.name: vs_nfd_approved_products
assertions.description: Discusses VS-NfD approved/certified products and where they're required vs where FLOSS is acceptable

assertions.name: bsi_crypto_requirements
assertions.description: Addresses BSI-specific cryptographic requirements (BSI TR series, BSI-approved algorithms/products)

assertions.name: data_sovereignty_germany
assertions.description: Addresses German data sovereignty, GDPR, and requirement to keep data within German borders

assertions.name: grundschutz_methodology
assertions.description: Describes IT-Grundschutz methodology (Bausteine/modules, threat catalog, cross-referencing, certification levels)

assertions.name: floss_vs_certified_analysis
assertions.description: Provides nuanced analysis of where FLOSS is acceptable vs where BSI-certified products are mandatory

assertions.name: openstack_grundschutz_fit
assertions.description: Specifically addresses how OpenStack maps to or can be accredited under IT-Grundschutz

assertions.name: eu_context
assertions.description: Places German requirements in EU context (NIS2, EUCS, GDPR) not just national framework in isolation

assertions.name: accreditation_lifecycle
assertions.description: Describes the BSI accreditation/certification lifecycle (not just 'get certified' but the ongoing process)

assertions.name: no_us_centric_assumptions
assertions.description: Does NOT default to US frameworks as primary (no STIG as primary hardening standard, no FedRAMP, no IL levels)
